I say this: those people are delighted by the darkness of night and do not endure the evening's gloom; they fill the whole house with lamps and drive away the darkness with the light; but for us, it is not a handmade light, nor a lamp with moderate fire that chases away the darkness, but Christ himself who says 'I am the light of the world'; Isaiah also prophesied that the light would come to us, saying 'Jerusalem, be enlightened, for your light has come'; the Savior's grace has shone upon us, illuminating everything and loosening the gloomy cloud of ignorance; the devil had spread this cloud over us, not allowing anyone to lift their heart's eye to what is pure, and to measure the power of the Creator from the beauty of His creations; but now, those who were deceived have found great benefit; so that they would not gain anything from what seems to lead to salvation and rise to the freedom that is owed to their nature, the devil blinded their minds, as Paul says, so that the glory of the Gospel of Christ would not shine; but the cowardly one has failed in his hope; for the One who calls to salvation is greater; and so, a great multitude of the nations has been saved and has come to know their Creator, even if late

Those being instructed by the law towards knowledge of our Savior Jesus Christ, and the Jews being instructed by the doctrines through Moses, 'I abandoned, as it is written, the ways of my own vineyard, but the axles of my own tiller were plundered.' For they did not recognize the Word of God who became human for us, 'who became poor for us,' as Paul says, 'so that we might be enriched in him.' Therefore, the prophet Jeremiah also strongly rebukes them, saying, 'How can you say, "We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us?"' For the scribes' false pen has worked in vain, they were ashamed, impoverished, and captured. What wisdom is in them, since they rejected the Word of the Lord? They truly rejected the only-begotten Word of God, but he has become the head of the corner. The prophet says somewhere about them, 'The sons are foolish and not intelligent.' How does it not seem true to everyone that what was said about them is true? How are they not unintelligent and foolish, since, having the mystery of piety to be taught from prophetic readings, and being able to be wise about it through the Mosaic writings, they have become so neglectful of their own salvation that they do not even equal the efforts of the Gentiles in this regard? And indeed, God says somewhere to them, 'I set watchmen over you, and I said, "Listen to the sound of the trumpet," and I said, "We will not listen." Therefore, the nations heard, and the shepherds of the flocks among them.

Hear, earth, I bring evil upon this people, the fruit of their food, because they did not attend to my law and rejected my word. They truly rejected God's word, neither following the preaching of the holy apostles nor paying attention to the older books. For if they were truly concerned about being benefited, they should not have allowed their mind to be deceived by the name of law, but rather examined the things concerning the Savior through the holy ones, and also the things said by others in figures and types. One can see many images of things in the spiritual words, having a clear representation of our Savior's presence in the scripture. But already my mind is filled with various theories and memories of the holy Scripture. Nevertheless, one should consider the beginning of the word to be from the older things. And through the things that will make us more ready to believe, we should already proceed. Let us examine, if it seems good, the diet of Abraham and how and in what things the blessed Abraham existed. And let the threefold birth and sowing of Isaac be investigated.

For you will see, Jew, in these things and in, so to speak, the root of the nation, the mystery concerning our Savior, well and skillfully formed like bronze. But so that it may not seem to be forced, I will set before you the explanation through Moses and clearly unfold the history. You will understand more readily from us. Now Sarah was joined to Abraham, the ancestor of the nation, according to the law. He had a maidservant, an Egyptian named Hagar. But the free woman, born of free parents, was barren, seeing no fruit of her own womb, and was driven by a strong desire for children, burdened by her sorrow. What was most persuasive was present. For Abraham was eighty years old, and it was likely that the heat of nature for procreation had cooled in him. But Sarah, lamenting the barrenness of her womb and greatly distressed by her childlessness, had reached the end of her childbearing years. So, wise in her desire for children and the natural longing that was fading, she urged her husband to have relations with the maidservant, since she had not been deemed worthy of legitimate children, and even if it meant being seen as the father of illegitimate children. The divine Scripture says: 'Sarah, Abraham's wife, did not bear him children, but he had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar. Sarah said to Abraham...'

Behold, the Lord has closed me so that I do not give birth. Enter your servant, so that you may have a child from her. And let no one think that I am being persuaded to pleasure or being led to intemperance through the words of Sarah to the patriarch. This was not her intention, but rather she was concerned about her inability to bear children, which she considered difficult and burdensome, unless perhaps it could happen through another. Such was Sarah's attitude towards her husband. And this plan was being led to its end by the patriarch. And a child, Ishmael, was born to him from the Egyptian woman. Meanwhile, the desires for the free woman were being deceived. For she thought that she would rejoice greatly in genuine childbirth, but instead, she was overcome with grief because she was unable to bear children. But God, the provider of all good hope and the one who has power over all things, had mercy on her and made the barren and childless woman, who had been deprived of the ability to bear children for a long time, fertile and suitable for childbirth. And he said to Abraham, 'Your wife Sarah will no longer be called Sarah, but her name will be Sarah. I will bless her and give you a child from her, and I will bless that child. And that child will become a nation, and kings of nations will come from him.' And Abraham fell on his face and laughed, saying to himself…

If to the hundred-year-old there will be a son, and Sarah, being ninety years old, will give birth? And God said to Abraham: Yes, behold, Sarah your wife will give birth to a son, and you will call his name Isaac. And I will establish my covenant with him as an eternal covenant, and with his seed after him. This promise to Abraham is true. Since the announced thing has reached its end and the barren woman has learned to give birth, and the child was already in sight, and the heir of the paternal houses was appearing, the maid, having a non-legitimate son from Abraham, Ishmael, was being driven away as no longer needed. And as she was fleeing, and had already become very far from her own home, an angel from heaven was calling out to her, saying: 'Hagar, maid of Sarah, where are you going?' And she says in response: 'I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sarah…'
pass_b_english: The darkness of night brings delight to those who are consumed by its shadows, and they cannot endure the gloom of evening. However, they attempt to drive away the darkness by filling their homes with lamps, and the light from these lamps chases away the shadows. For us, though, it is not a handmade light, nor a lamp with a moderate flame, that dispels the darkness, but Christ himself, who declares, 'I am the light of the world.' This is a truth that was also foretold by the prophet Isaiah, who cried out, 'Jerusalem, be enlightened, for your light has come.' The grace of our Savior has shone upon us, illuminating all things and dispelling the gloomy cloud of ignorance that had settled over us.

The devil had spread this cloud of ignorance over humanity, preventing anyone from lifting their heart's eye to what is pure and measuring the power of the Creator from the beauty of His creations. But now, those who were deceived have found great benefit in coming to know the truth. The devil had hoped to prevent them from gaining anything that would lead to salvation and rising to the freedom that is their birthright, but he has failed in his endeavor. For the One who calls us to salvation is greater than the devil, and a great multitude of people has been saved and has come to know their Creator, even if it was late in coming.

Those who were being instructed by the law towards knowledge of our Savior Jesus Christ, and the Jews who were being instructed by the doctrines through Moses, failed to recognize the Word of God who became human for us. As it is written, they abandoned the ways of their own vineyard, and the axles of their own tiller were plundered. The prophet Jeremiah strongly rebukes them, saying, 'How can you say, "We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us?"' For the scribes' false pen has worked in vain, and they were ashamed, impoverished, and captured.

What wisdom is in them, since they rejected the Word of the Lord? They truly rejected the only-begotten Word of God, but he has become the head of the corner. The prophet says somewhere about them, 'The sons are foolish and not intelligent.' How does it not seem true to everyone that what was said about them is true? They have become so neglectful of their own salvation that they do not even equal the efforts of the Gentiles in this regard. God says somewhere to them, 'I set watchmen over you, and I said, "Listen to the sound of the trumpet," and I said, "We will not listen." Therefore, the nations heard, and the shepherds of the flocks among them.

Hear, earth, for I am bringing evil upon this people, the fruit of their own food, because they have not attended to my law and have rejected my word. This rejection is not just a passive disregard, but an active refusal to follow the preaching of the holy apostles and to pay attention to the older books. If they were truly concerned about being benefited, they should not have allowed their minds to be deceived by the name of law, but rather should have examined the things concerning the Savior through the holy ones, and also the things said by others in figures and types.

One can see many images of things in the spiritual words, having a clear representation of our Savior's presence in the scripture. My mind is filled with various theories and memories of the holy Scripture, and I am compelled to consider the beginning of the word to be from the older things. Through the things that will make us more ready to believe, we should already proceed. Let us examine the diet of Abraham and how and in what things the blessed Abraham existed, and let the threefold birth and sowing of Isaac be investigated.

As we consider the story of Abraham and Sarah, we see the root of the nation and the mystery concerning our Savior, which is well and skillfully formed like bronze. The explanation of this mystery is found in the writings of Moses, and it is clearly unfolded in the history of the people. By examining this history, we can gain a deeper understanding of the events that transpired. Sarah, the wife of Abraham, was joined to him according to the law, but she was barren and had no children. Abraham, being eighty years old, had likely reached the end of his childbearing years, and the heat of nature for procreation had cooled in him.

Despite this, Sarah's desire for children remained strong, and she was burdened by her sorrow. She urged her husband to have relations with their maidservant, Hagar, an Egyptian woman, since she had not been deemed worthy of legitimate children. This decision was motivated by Sarah's love of children and her desire to have a family. The divine Scripture records this event, stating that Sarah, Abraham's wife, did not bear him children, but he had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar, and Sarah said to Abraham...

The Lord had closed Sarah's womb, preventing her from bearing children. She told Abraham to enter into a relationship with her servant, so that he might have a child through her. However, this was not a matter of Sarah being persuaded to indulge in pleasure or being led into intemperance through her words to the patriarch. Rather, she was concerned about her inability to bear children, which she found difficult and burdensome. Such was Sarah's attitude towards her husband, and this plan was being led to its end by the patriarch. As a result, a child named Ishmael was born to Abraham from the Egyptian woman.

Meanwhile, Sarah's desires for a child were being deceived, and she thought that she would rejoice greatly in genuine childbirth. However, she was overcome with grief because she was unable to bear children. But God, the provider of all good hope and the one who has power over all things, had mercy on her and made the barren and childless woman fertile and suitable for childbirth. He then spoke to Abraham, saying, 'Your wife Sarah will no longer be called Sarah, but her name will be Sarah. I will bless her and give you a child from her, and I will bless that child. And that child will become a nation, and kings of nations will come from him.' Upon hearing this, Abraham fell on his face and laughed, saying to himself…

When Abraham was a hundred years old, would he have a son, and would Sarah, at the age of ninety, give birth? God spoke to Abraham, saying, 'Yes, indeed, your wife Sarah will bear a son, and you will name him Isaac.' This promise, made to Abraham, was a genuine one. As the events that had been announced reached their fulfillment, and the barren woman had learned to give birth, the child was already in sight, and the heir of the paternal household was apparent. Consequently, the maid, who had a non-legitimate son from Abraham, Ishmael, was being driven away as no longer needed.

As she fled, and had already become very far from her own home, an angel from heaven called out to her, saying, 'Hagar, maid of Sarah, where are you going?' And she replied, 'I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sarah…'
